blind defect hunt (agents/art-one-universe.md, rule 4): a fresh reviewer given only the picture and its 4x crops named nothing

Sunrise peach and soft blue sky, cloud white, brass gold and warm oak; warm white and amber for the person's glass, brown leather and moss green for his clothes; emerald for Ouro; jade, amber and sea-blue for the three agents; one red cap.

- No third arm, no extra or missing limbs and no fused legs.

35 mm lens, premium animated-film render, natural film colour. Eye level: just above the person's head, as if we stand on the stern step behind them. The upper left stays calm envelope glass and sky.

- What: Ari, as a faceless adult person from the shared universe, standing at the bow and looking out at the horizon.

A faint warm inner light, warm white turning amber at the core, shows mostly where the sunrise rim-lights the glass; the head never glows brightly and never reads as a lamp, bulb, egg or sphere; never saturated green.
- Build: natural adult proportions and an ordinary build: broad real shoulders, a head about one-seventh of the body height and shaped like a real human head, a visible neck rising from the shearling collar, a torso as long as a real adult's with the jacket hem at the hips, and arms and legs of natural length and thickness; never stretched tall and thin, never toy-like or doll-like.
- Height: the tallest figure by far; the top of Loop's head reaches the person's belt.
- Outfit: a well-cut dark-brown leather flight jacket with a cream shearling collar, charcoal wool trousers, brown leather boots and the brown leather flying mittens, and a deep moss-green wool scarf wrapped once at the neck with both ends streaming back toward the stern (left of frame) in the wind, behind the shoulders and away from both arms.
- Expression: faceless; calm confidence shown by the body: upright, shoulders square and relaxed, chin level toward the horizon, weight settled evenly on both feet.
- Pose: standing at the bow rail, both feet flat on the deck planks inside the rail.
- Limbs: exactly two arms, each from its own shoulder, and two legs.
- Hands: brown leather flying mittens sized for an adult hand, each with one thumb, never separate fingers. Near (left) mitten: closed round the barrel of a short, closed brass spyglass, lowered at the hip, the spyglass clearly gripped. Far (right) mitten: resting closed on the brass rail cap in front of the person.

- Outfit: none; he is the pet, not a mascot.
- Expression: content and alert, enjoying the wind, eyes soft.

- Hands: none.

- What: Loop, the helmsman agent, a small robot.
- Material: smooth, seamless pale-jade glass lit softly from within, brass joints, a dark rounded visor, a round brass ear disc and a tiny brass antenna with an emerald bead.
- Height: the top of his head reaches the person's belt; the tallest agent.
- Outfit: brass aviator goggles pushed up on his forehead and a short green flying scarf streaming back toward the stern in the wind.
- Expression: focused: his visor shows only two soft glowing oval eyes held level and steady on the course ahead, and the rest of the visor is plain dark glass; his body leans a little into the wheel.

- Limbs: exactly two arms and two legs.
- Hands: near mitten closed round the handle peg at ten o'clock on the wheel's rim; far mitten closed round the handle peg at two o'clock, both visibly attached to his arms.
- Facing: body faces the bow (right of frame); head turned three-quarters toward the camera so his visor and both eyes read.

The ladder is turned three-quarters toward the camera, so we see the rigger's back and both shoulders, and both arms and both legs read clearly.
- Limbs: exactly two arms and two legs.
- Hands: both arms raised, the left mitten closed round the rung above its head near the left rope, the right mitten closed round the same rung near the right rope, both arms and both mittens fully visible, each attached to its own shoulder.
- Facing: back three-quarters to the camera, facing the ladder; head turned over its shoulder three-quarters toward the camera so both eyes read.

### The engineer
- What: a small agent keeping the engine trimmed.
- Material: smooth, seamless sea-blue glass lit softly from within, brass joints, a dark rounded visor, and a plain smooth round top to its head with nothing attached to it.
- Height: about Loop's height; kneeling, so its head is level with the valve handwheel.
- Outfit: a brown leather work apron with a small wrench in its pocket.
- Expression: intent: its visor shows only two soft glowing eyes lowered steadily toward the valve, held level, and the rest of the visor is plain dark glass; its shoulders lean in over the work.
- Pose: kneeling on both knees on the open deck at lower left, both knees and both boots visible on the planks. The deck between the engineer and the wheel is open planks, with no low wall, console or box.
- Limbs: exactly two arms and two legs.
- Hands: both mittens, each with one thumb, closed on the rim of the valve handwheel, turning it.
- Facing: three-quarters toward the camera, looking down at the valve.

## Props
- Ship's wheel: wooden, with a brass hub, on a brass pedestal mid-left. Its axle runs fore and aft, so from this camera the wheel is a narrow, nearly edge-on ellipse with visible spokes and handle pegs; its lowest handle peg clears the deck.
- Spyglass: short, brass and closed, in the person's near mitten at the hip.
- Rope ladder: two side ropes with wooden rungs, tied to brass fittings on the rail and on the envelope's rim band; every rope ends in a visible brass fitting at both ends.
- Valve: a ship's deck valve: a small brass handwheel lying flat on top of an upright brass valve body whose wide round base flange is bolted flat to the deck planks with a ring of brass bolts, its pipe running down through the deck; nothing else lies on the deck beside it.
- Envelope: a long glass envelope with brass ribs filling the top edge; the gondola hangs under it on ropes from brass fittings, every rope attached at both ends.

## Setting
A glass-and-brass airship gondola with one flat, open oak deck on a single level, enclosed on every side by a brass rail with posts and teal-glass lattice panels, sailing above a sea of clouds with snowy peaks. The wind blows from the bow, so everything soft streams back toward the stern (left of frame): both scarves and the cap's pom-pom.

## Light
Low golden sunrise from the right is the key light on every figure, with warm rim light on their right edges and a soft contact shadow under every foot, every knee and under Ouro. The person's warm inner light is soft, never a neon glow. Ouro's inner glow spills a little green onto the brass rail. A few sparkling glints are welcome on the envelope glass and the brass, never inside the figures' glass and never a glitter glaze over the picture.

## Palette
Sunrise peach and soft blue sky, cloud white, brass gold and warm oak; warm white and amber for the person's glass, brown leather and moss green for his clothes and mittens; emerald for Ouro; jade, amber and sea-blue for the three agents; one red cap.

## Must not
- No third arm, no extra or missing limbs and no fused legs.
- No separate fingers, no pointing gesture and no thumbs-up: mitten hands only.
- No stretched, tall-and-thin or stick-figure person; no green person; no bulb, egg or sphere head and no missing neck.
- No text, letters, numbers, logos or symbols.
- No emoji faces on visors: no ">" or "<" eyes, no "^ ^" crescent eyes, no tongues, no winks; no mouth, smile or grin line on any visor.
- No glitter specks or sparkle dots inside any glass body.
- No low curved wall, console or hatch box on the deck.
- No comic or cartoon styling: no outlines, no exaggerated squash and stretch.
- No glowing trails or lines of light.
- No electronics of any age: brass instruments only.
- No tiles, cells or facets on the glass bodies.
- No two agents alike in colour, outfit or expression.
- No figure facing the camera full on.
- No image fades or vignettes.
- No figure's feet hidden behind a box or hatch.
- No climbing figure with one arm hidden: both of the rigger's arms show.
- No wires, hooks, strings or antennas on the engineer's head.
- No loose objects, cones or capped pipe stubs lying on the deck.
- No stand, plinth or plate under Ouro.

Three candidates, each generated whole at 1536x1024, quality high. The chosen one is outpainted on both sides to a 3072x1024 master, which ships whole, as a 1536x512 header and as a 5:3 phone crop centred on the cast. The night twin is a relight of the chosen picture: the same frame, figures and poses under a night sky.
